chain_focus: AI-enabled drug discovery, precision medicine, autonomous laboratories, and the omics data platforms that feed biological models. The chain follows compute and cloud infrastructure into scientific software and AI-native discovery platforms, then into diagnostics, drug programs, and named biopharma customers.

AMD Instinct MI355X (CDNA4) generation — the current-shipping Instinct accelerator on HBM3E and TSMC N3/CoWoS, deployed across cloud/enterprise/sovereign/supercomputing customers (Microsoft, Oracle, Meta) via ODMs. Prior generation to MI450/Helios (which moves to HBM4 + rack-scale); separated so the MI355X->MI450 transition delta is visible.

AMD Instinct MI450 / Helios rack-scale generation (CDNA, HBM4) — from fab tools and HBM4 through TSMC N2/N3 fabrication and CoWoS/SoIC packaging to the Helios rack (Instinct MI450 GPU + EPYC Venice CPU, Ethernet/UALink scale-out) and its anchor customers Meta (6GW multi-gen deal), OpenAI, Microsoft and Oracle. Generation-separated from the prior MI300/MI355X lineage.

AWS Trainium2 generation (Annapurna Labs design, HBM3E, 400G optical scale-out at ~1:4 attach) — vertically integrated from fab tools and HBM3E through TSMC fabrication, ASIC co-design partners (Marvell, Alchip) and CoWoS packaging to the Trainium2 UltraServer (NeuronLink scale-up, EFA/Nitro) deployed in AWS for its anchor AI-lab customer Anthropic (Project Rainier). Graviton (Arm) is the host CPU. Generation-separated from the future Trainium3.

AWS Trainium3 generation (Annapurna Labs design) — successor to Trainium2 on a more advanced TSMC node with HBM4 and copper+optical scale-out. Vertically integrated through Marvell/Alchip co-design, CoWoS packaging and Graviton (Arm) host to the Trainium3 UltraServer deployed in AWS for Anthropic. Forward-looking: limited grounded data until a dedicated AWS/Amazon or Marvell-Trainium transcript arrives.
custom AI ASIC (XPU) platform — hyperscaler-custom silicon for Google, Meta, and cloud AI inference/training

company: AMD / Intel / ARM (Graviton, Axion, Grace, Cobalt)
chain_focus: AI data center CPU — AMD EPYC Turin, Intel Xeon Scalable/Granite Rapids, AWS Graviton4, Google Axion, NVIDIA Grace (GB200/GH200), Microsoft Cobalt — the host processors paired with GPUs in AI training and inference servers

Advanced semiconductor foundry — contract wafer fabrication for AI chips at leading-edge nodes (TSMC N3/N2, Samsung SF3/SF2, Intel 18A). Trace from equipment suppliers (ASML EUV, Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA, Tokyo Electron) and raw materials (silicon wafers from Shin-Etsu/SUMCO, photoresist from JSR/Shin-Etsu/TOK, process chemicals) through foundry fabs (TSMC, Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry, GlobalFoundries, SMIC) to fabless chip designers — AI accelerators (NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Marvell, Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Microsoft Maia) and logic chips — then on to packaging (CoWoS, SoIC) and final hyperscaler/OEM customers.

HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) — DRAM die fabrication, TSV stacking, and CoWoS integration for AI GPU/XPU accelerators

MLCC (Multi-Layer Ceramic Capacitors) for AI server power delivery — high-capacitance (1uF-100uF range) ceramic decoupling capacitors mounted on GPU accelerator cards (each H100/B200 uses ~10,000+ MLCCs) and server motherboards for power delivery network (PDN) stabilization. Trace from BaTiO3 raw material and Ni powder through MLCC manufacturing (Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, TDK, Yageo, Taiyo Yuden) to server/GPU card OEM assemblers and final hyperscaler buyers.

company: Samsung / SK Hynix / Micron / Kioxia / Sandisk

From GPU suppliers and server ODMs through neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe, Lambda, NScale, Together AI) to AI-lab tenants (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral). Demand-side lens; shares the GPU-maker hubs with the accelerator chains.

AI datacenter power delivery and cooling infrastructure — the full stack from grid-level transformers (GE Vernova, ABB) and UPS/PDU systems (Vertiv, Eaton, Schneider Electric) through server-level power supplies (Delta Electronics, Lite-On) and GPU voltage regulators/VRMs (Monolithic Power Systems, Vicor) on one side; and rack/row liquid cooling (Vertiv, CoolIT, Asetek), heat exchangers (Alfa Laval), and immersion cooling (LiquidStack, Submer) on the other. End customers are hyperscalers building AI training/inference datacenters.

Power semiconductors for AI server power delivery — SiC / GaN / silicon power devices, gate drivers and VRMs that convert grid / 48V down to the GPU. From SiC/GaN substrates through power-device makers (Infineon, onsemi, STMicroelectronics, Navitas, Power Integrations, Renesas, Monolithic Power Systems, Vicor, TI, ADI) to server power and the GPU board. Power-silicon lens; shares hubs (Infineon / MPS / Vicor / Delta / Vertiv) with power_cooling.

Google TPU v8i (inference) generation — the inference-optimized v8 SKU: leaner HBM4 capacity, no OCS scale-up, efficiency-focused serving. Host CPU migrates from x86 to custom Arm Axion 2. From fab tools and HBM4 through TSMC fabrication, Broadcom co-design and CoWoS packaging to inference-serving racks for Gemini and Anthropic in Google Cloud. Workload-separated from the training SKU TPU v8t (which carries far more HBM and optical/OCS content per unit — the key investment delta).

Google TPU v8t (training) generation — the training-optimized v8 SKU with high HBM4 capacity and heavy optical/OCS scale-up interconnect. Host CPU migrates from x86 to custom Arm Axion 2. From fab tools and HBM4 through TSMC fabrication, Broadcom co-design and CoWoS packaging to OCS-interconnected training pods serving Google DeepMind (Gemini training) and Anthropic. Generation- and workload-separated from TPU v7 (Ironwood) and the inference SKU TPU v8i.
